task.title: Replace the web handler's positional capability list with an options struct
task.description:
webui.newHandler reached twelve positional parameters across two consecutive stories: ten when the history view added TaskHistoryReader, twelve when the optimistic web queue added SyncStateReporter and SyncModeSetter. Two pairs in that list are structurally identical. TaskDeleter and TaskRestorer are both func(context.Context, string) (core.MutationResult, error); TaskDependencyAdder and TaskDependencyRemover are both func(context.Context, string, string) (core.MutationResult, error). Each pair is adjacent, which is exactly where transposition errors happen.

Go's assignability rules would catch a swap between two values already declared as the named types, because both are defined types and neither converts to the other implicitly. But every call site passes bare function literals, whose types are unnamed and therefore assignable to either name. The compiler cannot see the mistake.

This was measured rather than assumed. Swapping the delete and restore literals in runServe compiles, and go test ./... -count=1 stays green across every package, while DELETE /api/tasks/{id} on the board answers HTTP 400 "cannot restore an active task" and the card is never deleted. A fully broken board delete ships with no signal.

The dependency pair is not exposed the same way. TestRunServeMutatesDependenciesThroughWebRoutes drives both routes and asserts the recorded operation kind, so a swap there fails. There is no serve-level test for the board's delete or restore route at all, which is why only that pair's swap survives. The constructor's shape and the coverage gap are the same defect approached from two directions, and neither half is worth fixing alone: the options struct without the test leaves board delete unexercised, and the test without the struct leaves the next same-signature pair free to transpose.

Suggested shape, not binding: keep NewHandler, whose four parameters are all distinct and which roughly fifty test call sites use happily, and replace NewHandlerWithTaskMutations and NewHandlerWithSyncControl with one constructor taking a named-field options struct. That also retires the positional nil padding, where NewHandler passes eight nils and handler_test.go's historyHandler passes "unexpectedTaskPosition(t), nil, nil, nil, nil, read" with each nil meaningful only by position.

Do not start before the optimistic web mutation queue merges; the refactor rewrites the same call sites that branch is still changing.

Acceptance: transposing the delete and restore arguments in runServe either fails to compile or fails a test, and a serve-level test exercises the board's delete and restore routes end to end.
